A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

PC and sTM are markers of endothelial activation that are not modified during acute kidney injury (defined as a rise in serum creatinine or oliguria) and may independently predict mortality/non-recovery from acute kidney injury.
protein C and soluble thrombodulin are biomarkers that are predictive of acute kidney injury.
PC and sTM are not markers of AKI but are associated with the development of AKI.
The main takeaway from our work is that
protein C levels are lower in patients with acute kidney injury and that this could be a marker of endothelial dysfunction.
protein C and soluble thrombodulin levels can predict acute kidney injury in critically ill patients.
protein C levels can predict mortality and non-renal recovery in patients with acute kidney injury.
